extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in enumerative combinatorics / generating functions
extracted.subtask_description: Exercises and notes for Chapter 4 (rational and related generating functions) asking students to prove rationality/nonrationality, derive explicit generating functions, show quasipolynomial behaviour, solve recurrences, and compute combinatorial counting formulas. Primarily problem statements that specify the required form or property of solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure of rational functions under addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F(x) and G(x) be rational functions. Is it true that F(x) + G(x) is also rational?

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of rational power series with integer coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose f(x)=sum_{n>=0} a_n x^n is a rational function with integer coefficients a_n. Show that we can write f(x)=P(x)/Q(x), where P and Q are relatively prime (over Q[x]) polynomials with integer coefficients such that Q(0)=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require P,Q ∈ Z[x], gcd(P,Q)=1 over Q[x], and normalization Q(0)=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator nonvanishing at origin for multivariate rational series
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose f(x1,...,xn) is a formal power series representing a rational function P/Q where P and Q are relatively prime polynomials. Show that Q(0,0,...,0) ≠ 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational-function coefficient-periodicity criterion (characteristic function trick)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f(x)=sum_{n>=0} a_n x^n is rational and χ: C→{0,1} is defined by χ(a)=1 if a≠0 and 0 otherwise, then sum χ(a_n) x^n is also rational (hence its coefficients are eventually periodic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that indicator sequences of nonzero coefficients of rational one-variable power series are eventually periodic (Exercise 4.4(a)). The corresponding result is false in two variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hankel determinant finite-rank criterion for rationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Let H_n(a) be the Hankel determinant det(a_{i+j})_{0≤i,j≤n}. Show that the power series sum_{n>=0} a_n x^n is rational iff H_n(a)=0 for all sufficiently large n (equivalently the infinite Hankel matrix has finite rank).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use linear algebra to connect finite linear recurrences with vanishing Hankel determinants (Exercise 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to prove nonrationality of explicit series
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct or show examples of formal power series F(x) (e.g., products over i of (1-x^i)^{-b_i} etc.) that are not rational functions of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 7(a) asks to show a specific constructed F(x) is not rational; Exercise 7(b) asks to give contrasting examples where a similar construction is rational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences for logarithmic derivative representation
rubrics_metrics.description: For F(x)=sum_{n>=1} a_n x^n, establish equivalence of: (i) There exists a rational power series G(x) with F(x)=G'(x)/G(x); (ii) exp(sum_{n>=1} a_n x^n / n) is rational; (iii) there exist nonzero complex numbers α_i, β_j such that for all n >=1, a_n = sum_i α_i^n - sum_j β_j^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 8 lists these three equivalent conditions; the solution should show equivalence of the algebraic/logarithmic/exponential characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integer-value implies polynomial? (rational functions over Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F(x) is a rational function over Q such that F(n) ∈ Z for all n ∈ Z, does it follow that F(x) is a polynomial?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 9 asks to decide/justify whether integer-valued rational functions must be polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality from analyticity with only pole singularities and integer Taylor coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(z) be analytic on a disk and have only poles inside/on the boundary; if the Taylor coefficients a_n at 0 are integers, show the Taylor series is a rational function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 10: use analytic continuation/pole structure to deduce rationality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve linear recurrences explicitly or give simple descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given linear recurrences (various initial conditions and orders), compute explicit formulas for a_n or, when asked, give a simple description (e.g., using periodicity/modular decomposition) rather than a closed-form expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 11 contains multiple recurrence-solving tasks; for some complicated high-order recurrences the instruction is 'Rather than an explicit formula give a simple description'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain combinatorial appearances (pattern recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why a given combinatorial sequence (e.g., 1/9899 decimal expansion 0.0001020305... ) contains Fibonacci numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 12 requests a conceptual explanation linking the decimal construction to Fibonacci sequence generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Fibonacci number divisible by n
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that for every n ≥ 1 there exists a Fibonacci number F_k, k ≥ 1, divisible by n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13: requires use of periodicity of Fibonacci sequence modulo n (Pisano period) or pigeonhole principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct initial conditions to force composite sequence values
rubrics_metrics.description: Show we can choose integers a,b so that the recurrence f(0)=a,f(1)=b,f(n+1)=f(n)+f(n-1) yields f(n) composite for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14: constructive existence proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eventual polynomiality of counts from order ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Let I be an order ideal in N^m and f(n) be number of elements of I of rank n. Show f(n)=P(n) for sufficiently large n (i.e., eventual polynomiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 15 suggests Ehrhart-style counting / combinatorial arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting partitions with fixed part constraints — exact formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute exact formulas for counts of partitions of n with constraints like λ_3 = 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16: derive exact enumerative formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of two descent-polynomial generating functions (combinatorial identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Fn(x)=sum_{w∈A_n} x^{des(w)} and Gn(x)=sum_{w∈B_n} x^{des(w)} for two combinatorial sets A_n,B_n; show Fn(x)=Gn(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17(a) asks for combinatorial proof of equality of two generating polynomials enumerating descents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial derivation of polynomial sequences defined by functional equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Define polynomials p_n(u) by a generating-function identity and use combinatorial reasoning to find closed forms or properties (Exercise 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18 requests combinatorial interpretation to obtain the polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating function from nonlinear recurrence/product recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a function f: N→R with multiplicative recurrence f(n+2)=f(n+1) f(n) (or other nonlinear recurrences), find F(x)=sum f(n)x^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 19 asks to find the generating function F(x) of such sequences; may involve handling many initial-case distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count words avoiding forbidden factors via polynomial identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the number of words of length n over {N,E,W} avoiding EW and WE equals the number of nonzero coefficients of polynomial P_n(x)=prod_{j=1}^n (1 + x^j - x^{j+1}), and show all nonzero coefficients are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 20 requests combinatorial interpretation and coefficient-uniformity proof; points to Exercise 1.35(k) for related results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute generating function for unique tournament degree sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Define f(n) = number of unique tournament degree sequences on [n]; show that sum_{n>=0} f(n) x^n equals a specified rational expression and compute initial coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21 asks to derive the generating function and list first terms (explicit rational form given in exercise statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit formula and rationality for binomial-sum sequences f_α(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f_α(n)=sum_{k=0}^n binom(n,k) α^k; find explicit formula for f_α(n) and show F_α(x)=sum f_α(n) x^n is rational; identify special α requiring separate treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22: compute closed form and generating function, note exceptional α values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix-product representation and rationality of coefficient-counting sequences over finite fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f(x) ∈ F_q[x1,...,x_k] and a target coefficient α, show there exist integer matrices A_i and vectors u,v such that N_α(n) = u A_{a0} A_{a1} ... A_{ar} v where a0+ a1 q + ... + ar q^r is base-q expansion of n; deduce the rationality of generating function sum N_α(1+q+...+q^n) x^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 24: use automata/linear-algebra (transfer-matrix) method to prove rationality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic decomposition of coefficient-counting functions for polynomials over finite fields
rubrics_metrics.description: For k=1 case, show there exist periodic functions u(m), v(m) such that N_α(q^m - 1)=u(m) q^m + v(m) for all sufficiently large m; periods relate to field extension degree and multiplicities of factors of f(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 25(a)-(d): identify period d (degree of extension), multiplicity µ, primitivity, and give explicit examples illustrating periodic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotics and quasipolynomiality for number of p-groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit formulas for g_n(p) (number of isomorphism classes of groups of order p^n) for small n, show growth g_n(p)=p^{(27/??) n^3 + O(n^{5/2})} (exercise gives exponent form), and show for fixed n, g_n(p) is a quasipolynomial in p for p sufficiently large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 26: combines exact small-n formulas, asymptotic growth in n for fixed p, and quasipolynomiality in p for fixed n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality of word-count generating function for quotient monoids under relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M be quotient of free monoid X* by relations w_i = w_i'. For k=1 show F(x)=sum f(n) x^n is rational; show in general F(x) need not be rational; show F(x) is rational when M is commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 27(a)-(d): produce proofs and counterexamples; compute explicit F(x) for given relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality of trace-type generating functions for matrix word traces
rubrics_metrics.description: Given fixed n×n matrices A,B and α,β ∈ N^r, show Tr(x,y)=sum_{α,β∈N^r} t(α,β) x^α y^β is rational (t(α,β)=tr A^{α1} B^{β1} ... A^{αr} B^{βr}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 28 asks to compute denominator/explicit form in small examples (given A,B matrices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality question for (A^n B^n C^n)_{ij} generating function
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the generating function sum_{n>=1} (A^n B^n C^n)_{ij} x^n is rational for fixed i,j (true/false question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 29: evaluate using properties of matrix powers and noncommutativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit description of monoid generating function as rational function P/CF(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For E the monoid of N-solutions to linear equation x+y+2z−w=0, write E(x)=sum_{α∈E} x^α explicitly in the form P(x)/CF(E)(1 - x^β) (determine CF(E) and polynomial P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30: identify elements of the conductor CF(E) and build explicit rational form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasipolynomiality of counts of modular/congruence solutions for large modulus
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(n) be number of Z/nZ-solutions to a linear Diophantine congruence Φα≡0 (mod n). Show f(n) is a quasipolynomial for n sufficiently large (so sum f(n) x^n is rational).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 31: typical Ehrhart/quasi-polynomial behaviour in modular counting problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality of generating function for distinct-integer solutions monoid E*
rubrics_metrics.description: Let E* be set of N-solutions to Φα=0 with distinct integer components; show generating function E*(x)=sum_{α∈E*} x^α is rational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 32: uses structure of monoid of solutions to deduce rational form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superpolynomial growth and rational form for E_{Φ_n} monoid generators
rubrics_metrics.description: For special Φ_n (matrix with entries 1..n), show number of generators of monoid E_{Φ_n} grows faster than any polynomial in n; compute generating function E_{Φ^3}(x) as a rational function reduced to lowest terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 33: asymptotic combinatorial growth proof and explicit rational computation for small dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-property for pairs (Φ,β) and reciprocity of generating functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Define R-property: E_β(x) = (−1)^{corank(Φ)} x^d E_β(1/x) (Theorem 4.5.14 asserts (Φ,0) has R-property). Give necessary/sufficient conditions for (Φ,β) to have R-property and deduce consequences (e.g., when E_β(x)=0 or has same least denominator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 35(a)-(d): constructive and structural conditions, including existence of particular positive/negative integer solutions implying R-property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive (unimodular) triangulations and Ehrhart polynomial expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions: Does every integral polytope have a primitive triangulation? If Γ is a primitive triangulation of integer polytope P with f_i i-dimensional faces, express Ehrhart polynomial i(P,n) in terms of the f_i's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 36(a)-(b): relates triangulations, unimodularity, and Ehrhart coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational Laurent series decomposition via vertex support cones
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer polytope P and each vertex v define support cone C_v; show each F_v(x)=sum_{γ∈C_v∩Z^d} x^γ is a rational Laurent series and sum_v F_v(x) = sum_{γ∈P∩Z^d} x^γ (as a sum of rational functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 37(a)-(b) gives examples and requests proof of rationality and decomposition (includes provided small examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasipolynomiality for parameterized linear systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Φ(n) be integer-matrix polynomial in n and β(n) vector polynomial in n; if number f(n) of N-solutions is finite for each fixed n, show f(n) is a quasipolynomial for sufficiently large n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 38: extension of Ehrhart-type results to parameterized families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality of generating function for number of solutions to polynomial congruences mod p^n
rubrics_metrics.description: Given polynomials P_1,...,P_k ∈ Z[x1,...,xm] and prime p, let f(n) be number of solutions modulo p^n; show sum_{n>=1} f(n) x^n / n is rational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 39(b): relates p-adic counting and rationality (see Exercise 4.8 for equivalent forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster method functional equation and specializations; rationality when pattern set finite
rubrics_metrics.description: For a set L of forbidden factors, define cluster-generating-function C(x,t) and prove identity (4.52): sum_{clusters} t^{m_v(µ)} x^{|w|} = (1 - (sum x_i) - C(x,t-1))^{-1}. Specializations count words with given numbers of factors from L; if L finite and commuting variables, the equation represents a rational function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 40(a)-(c) gives the cluster method identity, its specializations, and the rationality conclusion when L finite and variables commute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autocorrelation polynomial formula for avoidance of a word
rubrics_metrics.description: Given word w of length ℓ with autocorrelation polynomial A_w(x), show generating function for number f(m) of words of length m avoiding w as factor satisfies sum_{m>=0} f(m) x^m = A_w(x) / ((1 - n x) A_w(x) + x^ℓ), where n is alphabet size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 40(d) states formula (4.53) and requests derivation using cluster/autocorrelation arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting nonattacking chess-piece placements: rational/quasipolynomial generating functions and asymptotics
rubrics_metrics.description: For B_k(n) number of ways to place k nonattacking queens on n×n board (and similar for bishops), derive explicit formulas for small k, show for fixed k that B_k(n) is a quasipolynomial in n (and the generating series sum B_k(n) x^n is rational), and give asymptotic forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 41 and 42: compute closed forms for B1,B2,B3, show factorial/asymptotic bounds and quasipolynomiality (period 2 for bishops).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating functions for constrained integer compositions/tuples
rubrics_metrics.description: Given N_{k,r}(n) number of n-tuples over [k] with no r consecutive equal entries, find explicit generating function F_{k,r}(x)=sum N_{k,r}(n) x^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 44: produce closed-form rational expression for F_{k,r}(x) with N_{k,r}(0)=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasipolynomiality of sequences defined by rational-function recurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions defined by recurrences f(n+m) = rational-function(n) combinations (e.g., Exercise 45: f(n+1) = ((n+2)/n) f(n) on domain) are quasipolynomials on their domain; analyze replacing rational factor by general R(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 45(a)-(b) requests proving quasipolynomial behaviour and exploring generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded integer linear-recurrence sequences are periodic and rationality vs natural boundary dichotomy
rubrics_metrics.description: If f: N→Z satisfies a linear recurrence with integer coefficients and is bounded, then f(n) is periodic. Also: if y is a power series with integer coefficients and radius of convergence 1, then y is either rational or has the unit circle as natural boundary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 46(a)-(c): prove periodicity via algebraic integer arguments and discuss analytic continuation vs natural boundary for integer-coefficient power series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition-count generating functions for vector partitions into k parts
rubrics_metrics.description: For α ∈ N^m, let f_k(α) be number of partitions of α into k N^m-parts; derive generating functions and relations among these functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 47 begins this line of partition enumeration problems; formulate generating function in terms of variables counting parts and sizes.
